vision.title: Vision
vision.content: Our vision is to advance sustainable and resilient infrastructure through innovative materials and structural engineering. We develop next-generation concrete technologies, intelligent monitoring systems, and life-cycle assessment methods to address the grand challenges of urbanization and climate change.

research.title: Research Directions
research.intro: Our research focuses on four interconnected pillars that span the full lifecycle of concrete infrastructure — from construction and strengthening to intelligent monitoring and long-term durability.

directions.name: Rehabilitation
directions.short: Advanced strengthening and repair of existing concrete structures using UHPC, FRP, and novel cementitious composites.
directions.detail: We develop innovative rehabilitation techniques for aging and damaged concrete infrastructure. Our work encompasses ultra-high performance concrete (UHPC) overlays and jackets, fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) strengthening systems, and novel repair materials with enhanced durability. We combine full-scale experimental testing with computational modeling to establish design guidelines for structural rehabilitation.

directions.name: Assembly
directions.short: Prefabrication, modular construction, and 3D concrete printing for accelerated and sustainable building processes.
directions.detail: Our assembly research explores the frontiers of automated and modular concrete construction. We investigate 3D concrete printing with advanced cementitious materials, prefabricated UHPC components for accelerated bridge construction, and digital fabrication workflows. Our goal is to reduce construction time, material waste, and carbon footprint while improving quality control through industrialization.

directions.name: Intelligence
directions.short: AI-driven structural health monitoring, predictive modeling, and smart decision-support systems for infrastructure management.
directions.detail: We harness artificial intelligence and machine learning to create intelligent infrastructure systems. Our projects include computer vision-based crack detection and assessment, deep learning models for concrete mix design optimization, sensor networks for real-time structural health monitoring, and AI-assisted decision frameworks for maintenance prioritization. We bridge the gap between data science and civil engineering practice.

directions.name: Longevity
directions.short: Life-cycle assessment, durability enhancement, and sustainable materials for long-lasting concrete infrastructure.
directions.detail: Ensuring the long-term performance of concrete structures in aggressive environments is central to our longevity research. We study degradation mechanisms including corrosion, freeze-thaw, sulfate attack, and alkali-silica reaction. Our work develops service-life prediction models, accelerated testing protocols, and durable material formulations incorporating supplementary cementitious materials, recycled aggregates, and bio-inspired protective systems.
